body:
Discrete-form boundary conditions on the ice velocities don't work at the moment. The halo fills after each velocity update (`fill_halo_regions!(u)` in the explicit solver, and the per-substep fill in the split-explicit solver) are called without `clock` and `fields`. So a boundary condition like

```julia
@inline west_inflow(j, k, grid, clock, fields) = 0.05 * fields.ℵ[1, j, k]
u_bcs = FieldBoundaryConditions(grid, (Face(), Center(), nothing);
                                west = NormalFlowBoundaryCondition(west_inflow, discrete_form = true))
```

errors on the first time step with `MethodError: objects of type DiscreteBoundaryFunction ... are not callable`. This rules out open-boundary conditions whose inflow velocity depends on the ice state at the boundary.

This PR passes the same `clock` and `fields(model)` that `update_state!` uses to both fills. In the split-explicit solver, a small `fill_halo_arguments` helper builds the argument tuple, because distributed fills take the communication buffers before `clock, fields`.

The new test in `test_lateral_boundary_conditions.jl` takes one step with the boundary condition above, for the explicit solver (viscous rheology) and the split-explicit solver (EVP). It checks that u at the west face equals 0.05 ℵ. It errors on main and passes here.

Related: #188 touches the same fill in the split-explicit solver. Whichever goes in second will need a small rebase. The `communicate` path in #188 calls `fill_halo_regions!(u)` without clock either, so it would need the same arguments.

Closes #201.

title: Pass clock and fields to the ice-velocity halo fills
